role.altitude: The mechanical drafter keeps reading designs, choosing views, modifying models and judging manufacturability; typing BOM lines, filling title blocks, hunting where-used and re-keying BOMs into the ERP shrink.
skills_to_grow: Keeping part properties in PDM complete so drawings and BOMs fill themselves
role.ambitious_version: A drafter whose released designs reach the shop floor and the ERP the same day, with no copied lines.

tasks.short: Read the design model, choose the views, lay out and draw schematic, orthographic or angle views of components, assemblies and machines, add dimensions and fastening details, fill the title block and have the engineer check the drawing.

steps.what: Drafter reads the engineer's model and sketches and decides which views and sections the drawing needs
Drafter lays out and draws orthographic and angle views of components and assemblies on the sheet
Drafter adds dimensions, tolerances and fastening methods to the views
Drafter draws schematic diagrams showing the functional relationships of hydraulic, pneumatic or drive systems
Drafter fills in the title block: part number, material, finish and revision
Design engineer checks and approves the drawing

tasks.design: Drawing templates per part type in the CAD system place the standard views and sheet layout from the model, and dimensions the designer set in the model are pulled onto the views, so the drafter starts from a laid-out sheet. Symbol libraries cover the common schematic parts. The title block reads part number, material, finish and revision from the part's record in PDM. Choosing views, adding the dimensions that matter for manufacture and the engineer's check stay with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each sheet was laid out from scratch and title blocks were typed.
tasks.enabler_now: CAD drawing templates and PDM properties that fill title blocks.
tasks.still_hard: Showing a complex assembly so the shop floor reads it right the first time.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which dimension the machinist will look for.
tasks.altitude: Less setup per sheet; drawing judgement stays with the drafter.

reach.learn: Whether template sheets cut drawing questions from the shop.

evidence.claim: CAD systems project views from 3D models onto templates and fill title blocks from file properties.
No measured result for AI drafting was found; the design uses fixed CAD features only.

assumptions: Boundary: from the design model to the approved drawing; designing the part is the engineer's work.
Input contract for s2 and s3: 3D models from the design engineer, with key dimensions set in the model about half of the time; older 2D-only parts are drawn as today.
Input contract for s5: the part record in PDM with part number, material, finish and revision, created by the designer when the part is made.
Choosing views and schematics keep their full or nearly full time; the engineer's check is outside the drafter's savings.
research_questions: Do template sheets change how often drawings are returned by the checker?

incremental.description: Drafter maintains drawing templates and symbol libraries.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one-off machines with many 2D schematics; high: product families with repeat part types modelled in 3D.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Create bills of materials from the assembly, fill item numbers, materials and descriptions, add unmodelled items, check the BOM against the drawing, have it approved and get the approved BOM into the ERP.

steps.what: Drafter lists the parts and quantities from the assembly to create the bill of materials
Drafter types item numbers, materials and descriptions into the BOM
Drafter adds items that are not modelled, such as glue, cable ties and paint
Drafter checks the BOM against the drawing balloons and the model
Design engineer approves the final BOM for release
Drafter types the released BOM into the ERP

approvals.approved_version: BOM revision as released by the design engineer in s5; a later change needs a new revision and release

tasks.design: The CAD system builds the BOM table from the assembly structure with quantities, and PDM fills item number, material and description from each part's record. The drafter adds unmodelled items as lines on a standard list and checks that drawing balloons match the table, which the CAD shows side by side. After the engineer releases the revision in PDM, the PDM-to-ERP link posts exactly that BOM revision to the {ERP}, so nobody types it again.
tasks.previous_blocker: BOMs were typed from the model into a spreadsheet and again into the ERP.
tasks.enabler_now: Design software generates BOMs from the model, and PDM-to-ERP links post released BOMs.
tasks.still_hard: Parts bought by function where the supplier code is unknown at design time.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting that a fastener in the model will not be available.
tasks.altitude: Most BOM typing goes; release decisions stay with the engineer.

reach.learn: Whether ERP BOMs from PDM cut order errors.

evidence.claim: Design software generates reports, wire lists and bills of materials from the design.
A machine builder reports 25% shorter lead time and half as many production changes after moving to design software (no method given, not AI).

assumptions: Boundary: from the assembly model to the BOM in the ERP; ordering is purchasing's work.
Input contract for s1: the assembly structure in the drafter's own CAD model; assemblies drawn only in 2D (about 20%) are listed by hand; s1 is priced at that share.

Input contract for s2: part records in PDM created by designers with item number, material and description; purchased parts come from the purchased-part library; about 70% of lines have complete records; the rest are typed.
Input contract for s6: the PDM-to-ERP link built by the ERP and PDM administrator, posting released BOM revisions; about 90% of items map; the rest are fixed by hand.
The engineer's release is outside the drafter's savings.
unknowns: Whether the company runs PDM with a link to its ERP.
research_questions: Do BOM errors found at assembly fall?

already_counted.description: Drafter fixes BOM lines rejected by the ERP link.
Drafter completes part records that PDM flags as missing fields.

incremental.description: Drafter keeps the standard list of unmodelled items current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many 2D assemblies and incomplete part records; high: modelled product families with a working PDM-to-ERP link.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Have the problem reported, investigate it, find where the part is used, modify and revise designs to correct operating deficiencies or reduce production problems, update revisions, have the change approved and notify production and purchasing.

steps.what: Production or service staff report the operating or production problem on the change request form
Drafter investigates the deficiency with the engineer and the shop floor
Drafter finds every assembly and drawing where the part is used
Drafter modifies and revises the designs: model and drawings
Drafter updates revision blocks and writes the change description
Design engineer reviews and approves the final change package
Drafter mails production and purchasing about the released change

approvals.approved_version: change package as released by the design engineer in s6

tasks.design: Problems come in on a change request form in PDM with photos and the part number. PDM's where-used search lists every assembly and drawing that uses the part, and its revision scheme updates revision blocks when the drafter checks the files in. After the engineer releases the change, PDM notifies the production and purchasing staff subscribed to the affected items with a link to the released revision. Investigating the problem and changing the design stay with the drafter and engineer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Change requests came by mail, and where-used was searched by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: PDM systems with change forms, where-used search and release notifications.
tasks.still_hard: Changes that ripple into parts already made or in stock.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing from the fitter what really goes wrong at assembly.
tasks.altitude: Less searching and mailing; design changes stay with drafter and engineer.

reach.learn: Whether release notices reach purchasing before new orders go out.

evidence.claim: A machine builder reports half as many production changes after moving to design software (no method given, not AI).
PDM systems search where a part is used and notify subscribers when a revision is released.

assumptions: Boundary: from the problem report to the released change announced; making the changed part is outside.
Input contract for s3: model references kept by PDM for parts checked in there, about 90% of current designs; legacy 2D drawings are searched by hand.
Input contract for s7: the subscriber list per product family kept by the PDM administrator; staff not on the list are told by the drafter.
Investigating and modifying keep their full time; staff and engineer time are outside the drafter's savings.
research_questions: Do changed parts still get ordered at the old revision?

already_counted.description: Drafter checks where-used lists for legacy drawings outside PDM.

incremental.description: Drafter keeps item subscriptions current with the PDM administrator.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: changes to one-off machines with many legacy drawings; high: series products fully in PDM with many where-used links.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review and analyze specifications, sketches, drawings and related data, check applicable standards and design rules, look up earlier designs, assess factors affecting component designs and procedures, and settle open questions with the engineer.

steps.what: Drafter reviews and analyzes the specifications, customer requirements and the engineer's sketches

loop.input: The customer specification and requirement documents for the project.
loop.output: A list of design requirements, each with the page and paragraph it comes from.
loop.check: Every requirement must quote its source text with page number, or it is dropped; the drafter reads the specification sections that bear on the design.
loop.why_not_simpler: Specifications are free text in varying layouts; a search finds words, not requirements.

steps.what: Drafter checks which standards and company design rules apply

loop.input: The drafter's question and the company's own design guide and standards index.
loop.output: The design rules that apply, each quoted with its section reference.
loop.check: Every rule must quote a section of the design guide or standards index, or it is dropped; the drafter opens the cited section before using it.
loop.stop: One answer per question; no answer if nothing is cited.
loop.why_not_simpler: The design guide is long and its index does not match how drafters ask.

steps.what: Drafter looks up earlier similar designs and drawings
Drafter assesses factors affecting the component designs: materials, tolerances, manufacturing method and assembly procedures
Drafter settles open questions with the design engineer

tasks.design: A bounded step lists the requirements in a customer specification with the page each comes from, and an answer desk over the company's own design guide quotes the rules that apply with their section. PDM search by product family and properties finds earlier similar designs. Assessing materials, tolerances and manufacture and settling questions with the engineer stay with the drafter.
tasks.previous_blocker: Specifications and the design guide were read end to end for each project.
tasks.enabler_now: Design software assistants answer from verified documentation; models can quote requirements with page references.
tasks.still_hard: Requirements that conflict or are left unsaid.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a tolerance on paper cannot be made in the shop.
tasks.altitude: Less reading and searching; design judgement stays with the drafter.

reach.learn: Which design guide sections drafters ask about most.

evidence.claim: A design software assistant answers questions from verified documentation.
Language models can list requirements from a document with the page each comes from.

assumptions: Boundary: analysing inputs before drawing; drawing and BOMs are separate tasks.
Input contract for s1: customer specifications as searchable files; scanned or drawing-only inputs are read as today.
Input contract for s2: the company's design guide and standards index, kept by engineering; purchased standards are read in the standards viewer.
Input contract for s3: earlier designs in PDM with product family properties.
Assessment and talks keep their full time.
unknowns: How long typical customer specifications are.
research_questions: How often does the requirement list miss a requirement found later?

already_counted.description: Drafter reads source sections behind listed requirements and rules.

incremental.description: Drafter reports outdated design guide sections to engineering.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: short specifications and known product families; high: long customer specifications for new machine types.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
